title: Prevention Is Better Than Cure for AI Societal Risks
gist: fDi Intelligence op-ed excerpt by Wendy Cutler arguing the US should pre-emptively and inclusively address AI's everyday societal risks (unemployment, inequality, strain on community resources) rather than focus only on security, drawing the lesson from trade policy where ignored warnings led to a now-closed window.

insights.claim: The AI policy debate has intensified after leading voices in the technology called for a development slowdown to address safety concerns.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Calls for slowdown from industry leaders raise regulatory risk for AI developers.
insights.quote: after the technology’s leading voices called for a development slowdown to address safety concerns

insights.claim: Security matters sit at the top of US AI policy priorities as policymakers balance frontier risks with promised economic, educational, health and scientific gains.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Security-first framing shapes export controls and compute governance.
insights.quote: Security matters are paramount when it comes to AI

themes.theme: Everyday societal risks: jobs and inequality

insights.claim: For many Americans the more immediate AI risks are tangible everyday effects: unemployment, rising inequality and strain on community resources.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Labor displacement and inequality could drive populist backlash and redistributive policy affecting AI adopters.
insights.quote: the more immediate risks are tangible effects on their everyday life: unemployment, rising inequality and hitting community resources

insights.claim: The US should tackle AI's societal risks inclusively at the outset to avoid needing more drastic measures later.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Implies harsher future AI regulation if early mitigation fails, a tail risk for AI valuations.
insights.quote: avoiding the need to take more drastic steps later down the track

insights.claim: The author frames AI as a replay of trade policy, where warnings about societal harms were not taken seriously enough and the window for action has now closed, whereas for AI there is still time.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Trade-shock backlash (tariffs, protectionism) is a template for possible AI-displacement political backlash.
insights.quote: We’ve seen this movie before on trade, where similar warnings were sounded but not taken seriously enough.
